prerequisites: Basic notions in numerical simulation, including mastery of basic numerical methods and their underlying principles (stability, precision, convergence, etc.)
Introduction to the resolution of differential equations (PDE) by finite differences (LEPL1104 courses)

learning_outcomes.text: subsequently become knowledgeable users of finite element digital simulation computer tools in the various engineering disciplines

become aware of the digital problems that may arise during this use. In particular, the accent is placed on the analysis of the criteria which make it possible to choose the most suitable method and to estimate the validity of the results produced by the computer
choose a method taking into account precision and complexity requirements
create a small C program implementing the complete resolution of a problem by the finite element method in the various engineering disciplines
certify and validate the result of the simulation thus obtained
Contributes to the development, acquisition and evaluation of learning outcomes: AA 1.1, 1.2
Contributes to the development, acquisition and evaluation of learning outcomes: AA 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.6, 2.7
Contributes to the development, acquisition and evaluation of learning outcomes: AA 3.1, 3.2, 3.3
Contributes to the development, acquisition and evaluation of learning outcomes: AA 4.1, 4.4

syllabus_topics: Interpolation of a function on an unstructured mesh
Finite elements for elliptic equations: weak and discrete formulations, fundamental data structures
Best approximation theory: introduction to the theory of distributions, Sobolev spaces, Lax'Milgram's theorem, Céa's lemma, a priori and a posteriori error estimates
Generation of meshes: Delaunay triangulation, introduction to numerical geometry
Finite elements for advection'diffusion problems: Petrov'Galerkin methods
Techniques for solving large linear systems generated by the method: band solvers, frontal technique and conjugate gradient method
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained from continuous assessment (A=Average of marks for homework) and certificate evaluation (B=Exam, C=Project). The final grade is calculated as max((A+B+C)/3,(B+C)/2) if (B+C)/2 >= 10, otherwise it is (B+C)/2. A new version of homework and project cannot be submitted after the deadline.
degree: Bachelor in Engineering (Bachelier en sciences de l'ingénieur, orientation ingénieur civil) - FSA1BA
